# .github/

This repository's own continuous integration and the instruction files its review bots read. Nothing here is catalog content.

- `copilot-instructions.md`, `instructions/code-review.md` and `instructions/*.instructions.md` are rendered by the bot-instructions package and each names its generator in a comment. Change `[bot-instructions]` in the effective manifest and re-render, never the file.
- `instructions/code-review.md` is this repository's whole review doctrine. `AGENTS.md` § Code Review Rules is the directive line that sends Codex there, and `copilot-instructions.md` carries the same pointer for Copilot, plus the `severity` block.
- Every job runs on a GitHub-hosted runner: the AUR and Homebrew workflows read the fleet's `vars.CI_RUNNER_2V`, unset in this public repository, and fall back to `ubuntu-latest`.
- `own-catalog.yml` holds this repository to the same check a consumer gets by calling `catalog-check.yml`, the reusable workflow consumers call; keep caller content out of it.
- `skill-tests.yml` runs the suites [`../skills/AGENTS.md`](../skills/AGENTS.md) names, plus `tools/` and `hooks/`. Read [CI and merge rail](../docs/architecture/merge-rail.md) before changing job selection, proof reuse or aggregation. `ci-job-set --event-parity` requires equal pull-request and merge-group selections for the same paths. `CI` holds every lane the older aggregators hold, plus Preflight and Markdown. Preflight, Markdown, doc-limits, todo-ban and the secrets scan run on pull requests alone: document and work-marker budgets must not eject a merge group, and the scan judges the commits its pull request adds. The bot-instructions check runs on both events.
- `actions/change-class` is the composite action this repository's workflows read a change class from, and the one a consumer references as `vanillagreencom/kendex/.github/actions/change-class@main` in place of calling its vendored classifier, per [`../skills/harness-ci/references/wiring.md`](../skills/harness-ci/references/wiring.md) § Through the composite action. It wraps [`../skills/harness-ci/scripts/change-class`](../skills/harness-ci/scripts/change-class) and `harness-only --mode docs` and classifies nothing itself; it decides `lanes` from those two verdicts, and each lane's verdict from `lanes` and the paths a consumer's default-branch `.github/ci-lanes.conf` declares. `actions/change-class/proof` beside it asks GitHub, with the job token and `actions: read`, whether a passing run of the same workflow already tested the same tree, per [`../skills/harness-ci/references/wiring.md`](../skills/harness-ci/references/wiring.md) § Proof reuse; the action stands down what that run's record covers of the lanes the workflow says do the same work on every event, publishes the record as `proof_record`, and uploads this run's own record for the run after it. Its suites are [`../tools/tests/change-class-action.test.sh`](../tools/tests/change-class-action.test.sh) and [`../tools/tests/change-class-proof.test.sh`](../tools/tests/change-class-proof.test.sh). Its `classifier` input names the checkout the shipped scripts are read from, and `skill-tests.yml` passes a separate default-branch checkout, so the classifier and the orch contract it measures by are never the pull request's copies. The wrapper itself and the `tools/` files `tools/ci-job-set`'s `LANE_SOURCES` names do run from the pull request's tree: review holds them, and a change to any of them runs every lane. A change to the classifier is proved by the harness-ci suite.
- `refresh-consumer.yml` is the reusable workflow every consumer's refresh caller, [`../refresh/kendex-refresh.yml`](../refresh/kendex-refresh.yml), calls at a major tag such as `v1`. It runs nothing in this repository. Each run installs the release tagged on the commit `job.workflow_sha` names and runs the refresh scripts from that checkout; the major tag moves per [app-deploy](../.agents/skills/app-deploy/SKILL.md) step 4. Its suite is [`../skills/review-gate/tests/shared-refresh-workflow.test.sh`](../skills/review-gate/tests/shared-refresh-workflow.test.sh).
- `lock-record.yml` runs [`../tools/lock-record`](../tools/lock-record) on every push to `main` with a kendex built from that tree: it re-records `.kendex-lock.json` where a merge moved it and lands the record through the rolling pull request `kendex/lock`, armed with the lanes app's token from the `kendex` environment. The choice is [`../docs/decisions/D007-lock-record-on-main.md`](../docs/decisions/D007-lock-record-on-main.md); the script's suite is [`../crates/cli/tests/lock_record.rs`](../crates/cli/tests/lock_record.rs).
- `dependabot.yml` asks for Dependabot security updates only, grouped per manifest directory. The orch overseer triages each alert and a lane takes over its fix pull request, per [`../skills/orch/references/security-alerts.md`](../skills/orch/references/security-alerts.md).
- `release.yml` is [`../docs/RELEASING.md`](../docs/RELEASING.md), and `publish-npm.yml` its § Pi packages on npm, which states what renaming it breaks.
- `publish-aur.yml` and `publish-homebrew.yml` carry `packaging/` to the AUR and the Homebrew tap; triggers, the dry-run dispatch and the secrets each needs are [`../packaging/README.md`](../packaging/README.md) § Publishing. Neither is called by `release.yml`: a release is published as a draft and the recipe bump follows it.
